summary: Rows 1-28 are the 1984 anime's Part 1 (eps 1-22 = manga ch 1-25, heavily REORDERED) plus the start of Part 2 (eps 23-29 = the Fang Clan arc, ch 26-37, in manga order). The reorder is the whole story of this block: Toei held Shin's defeat back to the season finale, so eps 1-4 play ch 1-5 + 7 (Club's fight lifted out of Southern Cross into Dorado, Mr. Heart's out of Shin's palace into a prisoner escape), eps 6-8 play the Golan arc (ch 11-16), eps 11-13 the Warriors/Jackal arc (ch 17-25), and only ep 22 returns to the Southern Cross showdown (ch 6, 8-10) — a 17-episode back-jump. Eps 9-10 and 14-21 are the anime-original padding that fills the gap (A1, no anchors). 17 anchors delivered (ep 1 -> ch 1 through ep 28 -> ch 36); ep 5 is anchor-hostile (an anime-original episode whose only manga content is the Shin-betrayal backstory flashback, A44) and comes with a proposed type correction to filler. Flag #688 is a false alarm: MU, AniList, hokuto.fandom and hokutosite.com all use the same 245-chapter / 27-tankobon space, and MU's latest_chapter=71 is a release-record artifact, not an edition; MU's own coverage segment for THIS entry ('Vol 16, Chap 136 (1983 S1) / Vol 24, Chap 210 (1983 S2)') matches our stored terminals exactly.

anchor_hostile.why: Anime-original episode: Ken rides to a castle that does not exist in the manga (in the manga Shin is in Southern Cross from the start) and is trapped by Joker, an anime-only KING officer; the sole manga content is the Shin-betrayal backstory told as a flashback (manga ch 8's flashback pages), which A10 excludes from START and which is a first-time sliver inside an original plot — A44 position-less. Type correction to filler proposed (T28).

annotations.note: Toei lifted two Southern Cross fights forward into the King-arc block: Club (ch 5) is fought in Dorado instead of at the Southern Cross gate, Mr. Heart (ch 7) during a prisoner escape instead of in Shin's palace — hokutosite's KING-arc change list states both moves.
The Shin showdown is held back 17 episodes: ch 6 and 8-10 are animated only in the Part 1 finale, after 10 filler episodes built out of KING's anime-original army.

The one manga tie in an otherwise anime-original episode: the year-ago betrayal (Shin carving the seven scars, Yuria's choice) is pulled forward as a flashback from the ch 8 confrontation. Mandatory tie annotation under T28.
Taki is killed stealing water in ch 18; the anime keeps him alive (he recurs to ep 13) — one of the series' systematic 'children survive' changes noted by ja-WP.

GOLAN is renamed God's Army and made a KING vassal, the Colonel is introduced in ep 6, Ken lets himself be captured instead of storming God Land, and two guard floors are added — the ch 11-16 spine is intact underneath.

The Fang Clan arc runs in manga order but each episode adds anime-only material: the rescued food truck (23), the clan recruiting the men Rei beat (24), the birthday cake (25), Gibara's ambush squad (26), Gojiba's sacrifice raid (27) — all listed in hokutosite's Fang-arc change list.
Joker (anime-original) pulls Jackal out of Ken's reach, extending the chase the manga resolves inside ch 22.

type_corrections.note: T28 materiality: the episode's job is Ken's ride to Shin's anime-invented castle and Joker's fire trap — no manga pages are adapted in running order, only the Shin-betrayal backstory as a flashback (annotated as a graft on ch 8). ja-WP's episode table bolds ep 5 as anime-original; Toei's own synopsis describes only the castle/trap plot; the fandom King-arc page lists the castle-and-Joker ending under 'Anime & Manga Differences'. AFL and AFG both call it non-filler — Sean's call; flagged.

structure.notes: CHAPTER SPACE / flag #688 RESOLVED — there is no edition divergence. MangaUpdates' own record lists '27 Tankoubon Volumes (Complete)' and its anime-coverage segments for THIS entry read 'Vol 16, Chap 136 (1983 S1)' and 'Vol 24, Chap 210 (1983 S2)', i.e. exactly our stored terminals (ep 109 -> 136, ep 152 -> 210) in the same 245-chapter tankobon numbering AniList reports; hokuto.fandom runs HnK Chapter 1-245 with volume blocks identical to our stored boundaries (v1 1-8, v2 9-17, v3 18-26, v4 27-35, v5 36-44) and hokutosite.com states 'zen 245-wa'. MU's latest_chapter=71 is the chapter of MU's latest-DATED release records (a scanlation index), not an edition signal — the known MU trap. No conversion is needed anywhere in this block. CAUTION for the MU writer: MU's coverage string here holds FIVE work segments — '(1983/2026)', '(1983 S2)', '(1986 Movie/Legend of Raoh 1)', '(Legend of Raoh 2)', '(2026 S1)'. The 2026 remake segment ('Vol 5, Chap 38 (2026 S1)') is new and could be mis-picked by a naive parse; the segments to read for this entry are '(1983 S1)' and '(1983 S2)'. ROW IDENTITY: our 1-28 rows join 1:1 by title and date to ja-WP's 各話リスト (Part 1 = eps 1-22, Part 2 opens at ep 23) and to AFG's prose list; no numbering defect found in this range. STRUCTURE: eps 1-22 cover ch 1-25 but in a scrambled order — King ch 1-5 + 7 (eps 1-4), Golan ch 11-16 (eps 6-8), Warriors/Jackal ch 17-25 (eps 11-13), and only then the Southern Cross showdown ch 6 + 8-10 (ep 22); the anime made GOLAN and the Warriors into KING's vassals to justify it. Ten filler episodes fill the gap (9-10 Patra, 14-16 King's Disciples, 17-21 KING's army). From ep 23 the anime runs in manga order. SOURCE NOTE for the next task (rows 29-56): ja-WP's episode tables bold anime-original subtitles ('太字のサブタイトルはアニメオリジナルである') — bold in Part 1-4 = eps 5, 9, 10, 14-20, 25, 38, 78-82, 105, 109. It is a useful positive signal but NOT reliable in either direction: it bolds ep 25, which demonstrably adapts ch 28-29 (Ko's execution, Kemada's death), and it leaves ep 21 and ep 83 unbolded although both are ruled zero-canon. In rows 29-56 only ep 38 is bolded (AFL adds 41). AFG for this series is prose-only — no per-episode chapter column, just 'Season 1 ~ adapted from manga 1 to 25' and 'Season 2 ~ adapted from manga 26 to 83'. hokuto.fandom has only five HnK Episode pages (1, 2, 10, 23, 38), but its chapter pages carry per-chapter character lists and its CHARACTER infoboxes carry an 'appearances = Manga (ch. X-Y), Anime (ep. A-B)' reverse index that resolved most boundaries here (Madara 'ch. 32-33 / ep. 27' pinned ep 27 outright). That index has at least one error: Misumi is given as 'Anime (ep. 3)' when he is plainly ep 2 — corroborate it, never index-join it.
